items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I was the only white on the date, and this was -- well, the date was Joe Turner's, and the name of the album, which is a collector's item, is The Boss of the Blues.

ctx.x: Well, there is no date on the album, but I think it was around '55. I was called for a record date at Carnegie Hall rehearsal hall, that's where it took place and they had set up equipment there, and when I walked in, I was flabbergasted the people on the date. In the first place, I walked in - and I always walk in early to set up the drums; there was Walter Pope there, and we said greetings and Joe Newman was there, and we had just begun to know each other, really; and Lawrence Brown on trombone; Pete Brown on…
I was the only white on the date, and this was -- well, the date was Joe Turner's, and the name of the album, which is a collector's item, is The Boss of the Blues.

I think he had asked for all the musicians that they could reproduce from the old days in Kansas City in that association, and I was there because possibly, Joe Jones or somebody from Kansas City who had played with them, didn't, or couldn't make that date, and it took a lot of hello's and explanations -- nobody remembered that I was that kid in Kansas City, and I didn't get any credit on the album, that I was around at the time, so I fit in on that date, I put that badly. The arrangements were by Ernie Wilkins,…
